field_semantics.population_*: Observed or explicitly modelled population interval for the mapped boundary and date interval; null means that the source does not support a defensible interval.
field_semantics.saturation_*: Fraction of the interval judged to be a long-run local-food Malthusian equilibrium. Most historical observations are validation-only and therefore null here.
field_semantics.local_food_*: Interval for the share of food supplied locally. It is a review aid, not a model target.
field_semantics.coverage_fraction: Estimated fraction of the named boundary that can be deterministically mapped to EU5 locations.
field_semantics.status: candidate is source-reviewed but not promoted as a scale anchor; reviewed_validation is suitable for out-of-period or non-saturation validation; lower_bound is one-sided evidence; unresolved means an interval or boundary remains inadequate.

criteria: two-sided saturation interval with independent pressure evidence
mappable historical boundary with high-confidence EU5 overlap
no unresolved war, epidemic, migration, or census distortion
promotion_audit.decision: No Americas/Oceania record is promoted. Every source has either an unquantified saturation fraction, an out-of-period date, model-versus-census ambiguity, or contact/shock uncertainty; exact island boundaries remain validation-only.

records.label: Hohokam lower Salt River/Phoenix Basin
pressure_evidence: Large canal network and irrigated fields supported a dense, locally supplied agrarian population.
Tree-ring streamflow and settlement studies link demographic change to water availability.
records.boundary_description: Lower Salt River valley and Phoenix Basin Classic-period Hohokam settlement zone; not the full modern Phoenix metro area.
records.boundary_source: NPS Hohokam culture overview; streamflow/population reconstruction for the lower Salt River valley
records.notes: The interval is a deliberately conservative archaeological diagnostic and is not a 1337 saturation label. The EU5 province is an approximate crosswalk, so do not use this record as a global scale anchor.

records.label: Cahokia and the American Bottom
pressure_evidence: Urban core and surrounding floodplain settlements reached unusually high density.
Maize agriculture, fisheries and floodplain resources provided a local subsistence base, while the urban core had non-local exchange.
records.boundary_description: Cahokia core plus a conservative American Bottom regional hinterland; core-only estimates are not treated as land capacity.
records.boundary_source: Illinois State Archaeological Survey Cahokia synthesis; American Antiquity/geoarchaeological regional estimate
records.notes: The 20–50 thousand interval is for a regional population estimate, not a vetted equilibrium. Mapping is unresolved because the modern EU5 geography does not expose a defensible Cahokia boundary.

records.label: Mesa Verde and Four Corners Pueblo region
pressure_evidence: NPS synthesis reports tens of thousands across the Four Corners before thirteenth-century migrations.
Marginal dry-farming conditions and drought sensitivity are documented, but local saturation is not quantified.
records.boundary_description: Broad Four Corners cultural region, not the Mesa Verde National Park boundary alone.
records.boundary_source: National Park Service people and landscape history
records.notes: Population values are a screening interval only; no robust mapped boundary or saturation fraction has been found. Keep as a negative test for dryland productivity, not a calibration target.

records.label: Lake Titicaca raised-field agricultural basin
pressure_evidence: More than 82,000 hectares of raised fields are documented around the basin.
Raised fields, frost mitigation, camelid herding, fish and tuber/quinoa production provide a local food system.
records.boundary_description: Agricultural lake basin associated with the raised-field zone; exact hydrological and archaeological extent varies by study.
records.boundary_source: Erickson/Candler raised-field capacity reconstruction and regional raised-field survey
records.notes: The interval is a published/modelled capacity envelope, not an observed 1337 census. It is useful for testing whether the mechanistic model can represent intensive high-altitude food systems without importing historical cropland shares.

records.label: Casarabe settlement system, Llanos de Mojos
pressure_evidence: LiDAR and settlement modelling identify extensive causeways, canals, forest islands and managed landscapes.
Recent spatial modelling places most settlements in the ten-to-thirty-thousand range, with a wider regional envelope up to about one hundred thousand.
records.boundary_description: Mapped Casarabe cultural landscape in the Llanos de Mojos; published LiDAR study area is approximately 5,020 km2 and is not the whole basin.
records.boundary_source: Casarabe LiDAR settlement surveys and regional population modelling
records.notes: Boundary and chronology remain incomplete. Retain as a holdout landscape-engineering test; do not promote to scale until the mapped footprint and local saturation evidence are resolved.

records.label: Upper Xingu and southern Amazon managed landscape
pressure_evidence: Pre-contact geoglyphs, roads, ring villages and anthropogenic soils demonstrate large-scale landscape management.
Published regional estimates are broad and depend on settlement visibility and extrapolation.
records.boundary_description: Upper Xingu cultural-geographic region; the evidence is distributed across multiple study polygons rather than one administrative boundary.
records.boundary_source: Nature Communications geoglyph/settlement synthesis and Upper Xingu archaeology review
records.notes: The wide interval intentionally records source uncertainty; it is not a census and cannot supervise the global scale. Use for rank and uncertainty diagnostics only.

records.label: Marajo Island and estuarine Amazon
pressure_evidence: Earthworks, ponds and sites with at least hundreds to over one thousand residents show managed wetland food production.
Regional density estimates of roughly 5–10 people/km2 are too broad to form a vetted interval.
records.boundary_description: Marajo Island (approximately 23,000 km2) and selected estuarine archaeological sites; study polygons are not equivalent to the whole island.
records.boundary_source: Amazonian archaeology review and Marajo regional geography
records.notes: No population interval is entered deliberately. This packet prevents a weak density claim from being mistaken for a benchmark label.

records.label: Rapa Nui (Easter Island) food-limited population
pressure_evidence: Food-area and agroecological scenarios produce a wide but explicit pre-contact population range.
Small-island land, freshwater and marine constraints provide a natural carrying-capacity stress test.
records.boundary_description: Entire Rapa Nui island and nearshore resources.
records.boundary_source: Frontiers food-limitation model for Rapa Nui
records.notes: Out of the 1337 target period and therefore validation-only. The central value follows the authors' preferred scenario; the full interval is retained to test uncertainty propagation.

records.label: Tongatapu island
pressure_evidence: LiDAR and Bayesian settlement modelling estimate a dense pre-contact island population.
Taro, yam, breadfruit, coconut, fishing and agroforestry form a locally available food system.
records.boundary_description: Entire Tongatapu island; island boundary is unambiguous.
records.boundary_source: LiDAR/Bayesian archaeological population reconstruction
records.notes: The source estimates population, not saturation fraction; retain as an out-of-period validation case and do not fit the global scale to it.

records.label: Tonga archipelago
pressure_evidence: Archipelago total derived from island settlement reconstruction and the Tongatapu intensive landscape.
Inter-island exchange exists, so the archipelago is a better local-food test than the capital island alone but not an isolated single location.
records.boundary_description: Tonga island group, with boundary defined as the archipelago rather than modern administrative subunits.
records.boundary_source: Tonga LiDAR settlement reconstruction and regional archaeology
records.notes: Approximate archipelago crosswalk and heterogeneous island evidence; use for aggregation/rank diagnostics only.

records.label: Upolu, Samoa
pressure_evidence: Genetic-demographic reconstruction gives a large Upolu effective population and an independent demographic estimate near seventy thousand.
Island food production is based on taro, breadfruit, bananas, coconuts, pigs and marine resources.
records.boundary_description: Entire island of Upolu; not the state of Samoa or the wider Samoan archipelago.
records.boundary_source: Sear et al. Pacific population reconstruction table and archaeological context
records.notes: Effective population is not a census and the date interval is broad. Preserve the distinction in holdout evaluation; do not treat this as a saturation anchor.

records.label: Tahiti at European contact
pressure_evidence: Contact-era demographic reconstructions give approximately 110–180 thousand people on the island.
Intensive taro and breadfruit systems plus fisheries could support high density, but warfare and contact effects complicate saturation inference.
records.boundary_description: Entire Tahiti island.
records.boundary_source: Rallu/Pacific population reconstruction and contact-era synthesis
records.notes: Far outside 1337 and affected by contact-era uncertainty; use only as a food-system stress test.

records.label: Aotearoa New Zealand early Polynesian settlement
pressure_evidence: Radiocarbon and site-density studies constrain rapid settlement and later regional expansion.
No defensible continent-wide 1337 census interval was found that is independent of demographic assumptions.
records.boundary_description: Aotearoa/New Zealand islands; evidence is regional and cannot be mapped as one homogeneous location.
records.boundary_source: SPDRD/radiocarbon settlement studies
records.notes: Retained as a temporal/land-use validation case only; absent population interval is intentional.

records.label: Hawaiian archipelago pre-contact food-system lower bound
pressure_evidence: A food-system model finds that more than 800 thousand people could be supported by irrigated taro, dryland crops, agroforestry and marine foods.
This is a lower bound on modelled capacity rather than an observed 1337 population.
records.boundary_description: Hawaiian archipelago, with island-level ecological models aggregated to the group.
records.boundary_source: Nature Sustainability Hawaiian food-system carrying-capacity model
records.notes: Out of period and one-sided. Only test that the model does not systematically undershoot an intensive island food system; do not use as a scale anchor.

records.label: Rurutu, Austral Islands taro landscape
pressure_evidence: GIS reconstruction quantifies extensive irrigated taro terraces and food-growing land.
Published work does not support a stable total population interval independent of assumptions.
records.boundary_description: Entire Rurutu island (approximately 38.5 km2).
records.boundary_source: Journal of Anthropological Archaeology GIS taro-landscape reconstruction
records.notes: Spatial land-use diagnostic only; missing interval is intentional.

records.label: Ontong Java/Luangiua atoll
pressure_evidence: Taro-growing capacity model gives 2,450–6,195 people, while an independent early twentieth-century reconstruction gives approximately 5,000–5,500.
Atoll freshwater and land constraints make this a strong hostile-environment test.
records.boundary_description: Entire Ontong Java/Luangiua atoll; modern administrative boundary is approximately coextensive.
records.boundary_source: Archaeological taro carrying-capacity model and Hogbin population reconstruction
records.notes: The year range combines a model and a later ethnographic reconstruction; retain as a validation interval, not as a 1337 anchor.

records.label: Moorea island
pressure_evidence: Pacific demographic synthesis lists an archaeological population estimate of about 22,906 for Moorea.
Island valleys combine wet taro, breadfruit, coastal fishing and upland resources.
records.boundary_description: Entire Moorea island.
records.boundary_source: Sear et al. Pacific population reconstruction table
records.notes: The source is heterogeneous and largely outside 1337; use only as an island rank/uncertainty case.

records.label: Mangaia island
pressure_evidence: Pacific synthesis reports a carrying-capacity estimate near 19,548 for Mangaia.
Raised taro wetlands and a compact island boundary make food/area accounting testable.
records.boundary_description: Entire Mangaia island.
records.boundary_source: Sear et al. synthesis of Mangaia carrying-capacity work
records.notes: Model-derived and out of period; useful for testing intensive island agriculture, not for global calibration.

records.label: Rarotonga island
pressure_evidence: Pacific demographic synthesis reports approximately 12,998 people for Rarotonga.
Valley taro, breadfruit, coconut, pigs and fishing form the local food base.
records.boundary_description: Entire Rarotonga island.
records.boundary_source: Sear et al. Pacific population reconstruction table
records.notes: Out-of-period, heterogeneous estimate; retain as a compact island validation case.

records.label: Mangareva island
pressure_evidence: Pacific synthesis reports a modelled population of about 3,537 for Mangareva.
Small volcanic island resources and lagoon fisheries provide a constrained local-food test.
records.boundary_description: Entire Mangareva island, not the wider Gambier group.
records.boundary_source: Sear et al. Pacific population reconstruction table
records.notes: Out-of-period modelled value; use for small-island monotonicity and uncertainty checks only.
